Anyone who wants to speak must [register by Oct. 26](https://www.fda.gov/food/workshops-meetings-webinars-food-and-dietary-supplements/fda-public-meeting-challenges-and-solutions-lot-level-food-traceability-11062026?ref=foodsafetynews.com), and no same-day registration is allowed.[Written comments are due Dec. 6](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/09/2026-20720/challenges-and-solutions-in-lot-level-food-traceability-public-meeting?ref=foodsafetynews.com)in Docket No. FDA-2014-N-0053. The meeting is billed as a chance to talk about implementation. Read the notice closely and it is something narrower: A conversation about how to make the rule’s core requirement, the lot code, easier to live without.

So here is where the Food Traceability Rule stands, how it got here, and why, more than fifteen years after Congress ordered it, FDA cannot spend a dollar enforcing a single line of it.

Although the CDC is reporting only 27 illnesses in a Salmonella Telelkebir outbreak linked to oysters, the Virginia Department of Health has documented 55 patients across 19 states.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported on Oct. 19 the patients were spread across 12 states with five of them having been hospitalized. The Food and Drug Administration reported the same number in a recall notice for oysters harvested by the Little Wicomico Oyster Company from the Little Wicomico River.

The Virginia health department reports that the illnesses began in late May and run through Oct. 6. The CDC reports that five patients have required hospitalization. Georgia’s Department of Agriculture says Publix sold the recalled oysters as “James River Oysters” through Oct. 14, five days after the recall.

For the 27 patients reported by the CDC, 10 reported eating raw oysters. Tag and traceback records exist for seven. Two of the seven ate oysters from a single Virginia source and five from several, and the company’s Little Wicomico River oysters were the only oysters in common to the seven ill people included in traceback.
